steps.title: An incomplete brief
steps.observation: The reply offers two dresses and optional finishing touches, without requiring a size or colour first.

steps.title: A colour choice
steps.observation: There is no exact blue match for this occasion. The reply preserves the request and offers a way to explore other colours.

options.label: Blue / captured
options.prompt: Show me blue dresses. Keep the beach wedding and the same budget.

options.label: Black / live option
options.prompt: Show me black dresses. Keep the beach wedding and the same budget.

steps.title: One more requirement
steps.observation: Adding size 10 keeps the blue colour and occasion in place. The reply still reports no exact match.

steps.title: A deliberate change
steps.observation: Changing blue to navy returns Navy Maxi Dress at A$95. Size 10 is listed, and the budget remains A$200.

steps.title: A cheaper option?
steps.observation: The reply reports no lower-priced match while keeping the remaining requirements unchanged.

steps.title: The reason for a match
steps.observation: The answer names polyester and the recorded Beach Wedding occasion, with a link back to the product. It distinguishes catalogue details from fit or performance guarantees.

steps.title: Something already owned
steps.observation: The trousers become an owned styling reference with A$0 new purchase cost. Shirt alternatives disclose differences in occasion.

steps.title: Two purchases, one limit
steps.observation: The reply asks which shirt to use before matching a bag, instead of silently choosing one.

steps.title: A different total
steps.observation: The reply still needs a specific shirt. Changing the total does not resolve that product reference.

options.label: A$150 total / captured
options.prompt: Reduce the combined budget for the shirt and bag to A$150.

options.label: A$250 total / live option
options.prompt: Increase the combined budget for the shirt and bag to A$250.

steps.title: An example, not a selection
steps.observation: Naming Black Linen Shirt resolves the reference, but this reply includes bags that would exceed A$150 for the pair. The next prompt makes the remaining allowance explicit.

steps.title: The remaining allowance
steps.observation: The purchase plan now shows A$95 for the shirt example and A$55 left for a bag. The listed bag alternatives cost A$55 or less.

steps.title: The price of the pair
steps.observation: Black Linen Shirt costs A$95 and White Mini Clutch costs A$50. The reply calculates A$145 together and A$5 left from A$150.

steps.title: Several requirements
steps.observation: The reply finds no exact match for black dresses in size 10 under A$200. It keeps those requirements saved.

steps.title: Only the colour changes
steps.observation: Changing black to blue also returns no exact match. Size 10 and the A$200 limit stay in place.

steps.title: Permission to broaden
steps.observation: Explicitly allowing any colour and any listed size returns five dresses under A$200.

steps.title: A rejected suggestion
steps.observation: This reply treats the product rejection as an unverified requirement and asks how to continue. The capture preserves that unexpected clarification.

steps.title: A new shopping goal
steps.observation: Switching the goal returns Black Shoulder Bag at A$90 and Black Crossbody Bag at A$75. The new limit is A$100.

steps.title: The next question
steps.observation: The answer lists a zip closure and 30 × 22 × 8 cm dimensions. It labels those specifications as synthetic prototype data.

options.label: Product details / captured
options.prompt: What are the dimensions and closure of Black Shoulder Bag?

options.label: A cheaper bag / live option
options.prompt: Show me a cheaper bag than Black Shoulder Bag, keeping the same requirements.

steps.title: Browsing before sizing
steps.observation: The reply offers Black Platform Sandals at A$120 and Black Low-Top Sneakers at A$70, without requiring a size first.

steps.title: A specific product
steps.observation: The answer lists sizes 5 to 10 and distinguishes catalogue labels from measurements or a fit guarantee.

steps.title: A guarantee request
steps.observation: The reply explains why it cannot guarantee delivery tomorrow and gives catalogue limitations. It does not directly resolve waterproofing.

steps.title: Continuing the search
steps.observation: Removing the extra requirements returns the two black shoe options again, within the A$150 limit.

steps.title: Facts or another option?
steps.observation: The answer names leather and labels its construction and measurement details as synthetic prototype specifications.

options.label: Material details / captured
options.prompt: What material are Black Platform Sandals made from, and which details are unavailable?

options.label: A cheaper option / live option
options.prompt: Show me a cheaper alternative to Black Platform Sandals, keeping the same requirements.
